extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, policymakers, patent stakeholders (independent inventors, practitioners, Congress)
extracted.subtask_description: PPAC annual report guidance for evaluating and improving the U.S. patent system, covering patent quality, accessibility for independent inventors, IT/AI tools, PTAB interaction, and USPTO finances. Intended to guide USPTO policy, rulemaking, and operational priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving the reliability and durability of the patent right
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest on-going priority of the USPTO is issuing patents that are reliable and durable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reliable and durable patent right starts with a well-prepared application and examination that considers closest prior art and applies proper legal standards; should withstand challenges in district court and PTAB. Initiatives include closing gaps between Patents and PTAB (joint training, data sharing), investing in IT/AI for search and classification, and ensuring timely pendency. Any change in law/policy should be assessed against supporting innovation and societal benefit ('True North').

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanding the number of people who engage the U.S. patent system as inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand participation in the patent system, particularly in under-represented constituencies and geographies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include outreach (Council for Inclusive Innovation), STEM and IP education, mentoring, corporate diversity pledges, measuring inventorship via demographic data (IDEA Act), and supporting pro-se inventors via training and pro bono programs to increase inventorship and national competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being good financial stewards so that patent system is efficient, affordable and accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO should manage fees and finances to lower barriers and operate efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include appropriating fees collected but not appropriated for specific initiatives (quality and inclusion), expanding AIA fee-setting authority (including decoupling from entity size), monitoring filing/fee trends to sustain the fee model, and seeking appropriations that do not adversely affect other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support Independent Inventors (accessibility and affordability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support independent, micro-, and small-entity inventors to ensure the system is accessible and affordable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures include pro bono collaborations, StART training, Customer Ambassador program, considering patent small claims court to reduce litigation costs, avoiding fee-based barriers (e.g., to encourage DOCX), and tailoring AIA discretionary-denial guidance to consider unique challenges faced by independent inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify subject matter eligibility (Section 101) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter eligibility remains an area of uncertainty; USPTO guidance provides consistency but more is needed to clarify the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commend USPTO updates but continue updates, provide technical comments to Congress, update guidance as case law evolves, and work with courts to provide clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement a Patents–PTAB feedback loop
rubrics_metrics.description: Create robust feedback between patent examination (Patents) and the PTAB to improve consistency and patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include cross-surveys, joint training (e.g., training examiners on strengthening Examiner’s Answers and PTAB judges on new grounds), data sharing, and studying outcomes to identify repeat errors and training needs. Training modules should be public and deployed (FY2023 planned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and analyze PTAB/examination data to learn from invalidations
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect outcomes and mine data to understand why PTAB finds claims unpatentable and to identify improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automate data collection of PTAB outcomes (already implemented), enable data mining to find trends (e.g., missed prior art, inconsistent legal application), and study results to guide examiner training and system improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply consistent legal standards across examination and PTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure examiners and administrative patent judges apply law consistently from examination to final written decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide guidance that engages PTAB, update MPEP more frequently, and give online access to examiner training materials so practitioners and examiners align on case law updates and examination practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in IT and AI tools to improve classification and search
rubrics_metrics.description: Use IT and AI to improve effectiveness and efficiency of examination, including classification and prior art search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy tools like PE2E Search, MLTD similarity search, CPC auto-classification, and support examiner training. Continue investment, retire legacy tools, and leverage foreign patent databases and translations to expand prior art access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept DOCX as structured authoritative filing format
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept patent applications filed in DOCX format as a uniform processing format and consider the DOCX file to be the authoritative/evidentiary copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOCX enables instant feedback to detect mistakes, allows automatic document code detection and content reuse, and improves searching. Provide free training, delay non-DOCX surcharge to ease transition, provide backup PDF option, and promote DOCX without imposing fee barriers on under-resourced inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide PE2E Search and MLTD to examiners with training
rubrics_metrics.description: Equip and train all examiners on Patents End-To-End (PE2E) search tools, including AI-based 'Similarity Search' and 'More Like This Document' (MLTD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy web-based PE2E platform to all (~8,500 examiners), retire legacy tools, expand access to foreign patent filings and translations, and use AI models that consider title, abstract, claims, description, CPC, and citation data to return similar documents for improved prior art retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CPC auto-classification to route applications to appropriate examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize AI-based CPC auto-classification to identify CPC symbols associated with claimed subject matter in utility applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application of CPC auto-classification helps place applications with examiners best positioned to examine the cited art; explore additional uses of auto-classification in examination workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce pendency, with emphasis on design patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely examination is a component of a reliable and durable patent right; reduce pendency, especially for design patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO should invest resources to meet/exceed pendency goals, hire and train design examiners, consider AI search capabilities for design examiners, and pursue electronic publishing of granted design patents to speed processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address parallel proceedings and discretionary denials (AIA/Fintiv issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce burden of parallel district court and PTAB proceedings and clarify discretionary denials of institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop guidance via ANPRM on discretionary denials to reduce parallel proceedings, encourage early correction via PGR, consider the Independent Inventor's unique challenges, update Director review process guidance after RFC comments, and issue guidance on joinder in AIA cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider objective (secondary) considerations at IPR institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Study whether objective considerations supporting patentability (Graham factors) should be considered more fulsomely at the institution phase for certain patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly consider patents that have been copied by competitors to mitigate uncertainty and costs associated with a full AIA trial for patents covering products providing competitive advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide outreach and training for independent inventors (StART, Customer Ambassador, Inventor Hour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create and run targeted programs to help inventors prepare and navigate the patent system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs include StART (free 3-day online workshop for preparing nonprovisional utility applications), Customer Ambassador support after filing, PTAB 'New to PTAB?' webpages in multiple languages, 'Inventor Hour' webinars, and a PTAB pro bono program for under-resourced inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance accessibility via multilingual resources and pro bono services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide accessible PTAB and USPTO materials in multiple languages and offer pro bono legal counsel to under-resourced inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB 'New to PTAB?' pages are available in Spanish and German (with plans for more languages); expand PTAB pro bono to AIA proceedings; meet inventor organizations and gather feedback on assistance tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect demographic data to measure and inform innovation inclusion (IDEA Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect demographic information to visualize and inform decisions about who participates in invention and innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass IDEA Act to enable USPTO to collect demographic data; use patent+demographic data to identify underparticipation, set benchmarks, analyze gaps, and measure progress from initiatives like mentoring and corporate diversity pledges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use collected fees for intended purposes and request appropriation of reserved funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees collected should be appropriated and used for specific initiatives to improve patent reliability and expand inventor participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO should identify uses for previously collected but unavailable funds and request Congressional appropriation (preferably outside normal budget scoring). Identify specific purposes in appropriation requests (quality, inclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand and/or make permanent AIA fee setting authority and consider decoupling from entity size
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant or extend AIA fee-setting authority and allow USPTO discretion to decouple fee setting from entity size to lower barriers for Independent Inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend permanent authority or another 7–8 year grant and expansion to allow fee flexibility that could reduce barriers; monitor filing and fee rates to ensure sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide more frequent MPEP updates and public access to examiner training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Update the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) more frequently and publish examiner training materials online to align examiners and practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Last MPEP update was June 2020; more frequent updates and accessible training materials would positively impact application quality and consistent application of case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore patent small claims court to reduce litigation costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider creating a patent small claims court as an option to decrease litigation costs especially burdensome to independent inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess policy options and impacts on costs, fairness, and accessibility while ensuring the correct operation of examination and durability of issued patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid imposing fee-based barriers to encourage DOCX adoption; consider change management alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Discourage using fees as the primary lever to encourage DOCX filing because fees create barriers for under-resourced inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider change management principles and alternatives to fees to promote DOCX use while maintaining accessibility; the PPAC suggests additional non-fee incentives or supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage stakeholders and solicit public comment before policy changes (ANPRM/RFC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ANPRMs and Requests for Comments to solicit stakeholder input and improve clarity/transparency of USPTO practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC supports ANPRMs/RFCs for discretionary denials, Director review process, PTAB guidance on joinder, and other areas to ensure informed policymaking and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor filing, issue fee, and maintenance fee rates to ensure fee model sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuously monitor user behavior and fee payments to maintain sustainability of the USPTO fee funding model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monitoring to inform fee-setting, budgeting, and resource allocation; include in recommendations to Congress for appropriations and fee authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen Examiner’s Answers and PTAB judge training on administering new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Train examiners on strengthening Examiner’s Answers and train PTAB judges on when to administer a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB developed training and plans to unveil examiner and PTAB judge training modules (FY2023) to improve appeal outcomes and consistency between examination and PTAB practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automate PTAB decision outcome collection for trend analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB automated data collection of outcomes to enable mining of large numbers of decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use outcome tables to identify trends such as repeat erroneous rejections in certain technology areas; Patents plans to study these data (FY2023) to inform improvements.
